result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [validate_sdtmig()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: >- Check SDTM datasets with Pointblank's bundled SDTMIG conformance rules. twitter-card: title: >- [validate_sdtmig()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: >- Check SDTM datasets with Pointblank's bundled SDTMIG conformance rules. title: >- [validate_sdtmig()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Check SDTM datasets with Pointblank's bundled SDTMIG conformance rules. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check SDTM datasets with Pointblank's bundled SDTMIG conformance rules. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_submission.py#L3148-L3332){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature validate_sdtmig( datasets, version="3-4", ct_packages=None, define_xml=None, study_id=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Before SDTM datasets are submitted, they are checked for conformance to the SDTM Implementation Guide (SDTMIG). The `validate_sdtmig()` function does this with a catalog of 362 rules for SDTMIG 3.4 that comes with Pointblank, so it needs no other software and no network access. It returns a [`ConformanceReport`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport`) with the result of each rule. For the published CDISC and agency rules, use [`validate_cdisc_submission()`](`pointblank.validate_cdisc_submission`), which runs the CDISC CORE engine. The rules are of these types: - Record checks (221 rules) check the values of each record, such as that `SEX` uses the terms of its codelist, that dates are in the ISO 8601 format, that `AGE` isn't negative and that required variables aren't null. These rules give the failing records as findings. - Variable metadata checks (116 rules) check that the required variables of a domain are present, that variables have the right type and that they are in the right order. - Dataset contents checks (9 rules) check across the records of a dataset, such as that `STUDYID` has the same value in every record and that `AESEQ` is unique for each subject. - Dataset metadata checks (3 rules) check that every dataset has `STUDYID`, `DOMAIN` and (for subject-level data) `USUBJID`. - Domain presence checks (3 rules) check that the DM, TS and TA datasets are present. - Define-XML checks (12 rules) check the datasets against their Define-XML, such as that every variable is declared in it and that values are from the codelists that it declares. These rules need `define_xml=`, and are not applicable without it. Four of the rules are of `"Warning"` sensitivity: the presence of TA and of `USUBJID`, and the order of the identifier variables and of the sequence variable. All the others are of `"Error"` sensitivity. A rule for a domain that isn't one of the `datasets` (such as an AE rule when there's no AE dataset) has nothing to check, so it passes. The codelist checks ignore case, so `"m"` is accepted for `SEX`. Empty strings (which is how XPT files store missing character values) are treated as nulls. SUPP-- and RELREC datasets aren't checked by the rules that apply to all domains, since they have a different structure (with `RDOMAIN` in place of `DOMAIN`). The rules check each dataset on its own, so they don't check that the subjects of one dataset are in DM. For that, use the `"validate"` engine of the `SubmissionPackage` method [`validate_conformance()`](`pointblank.SubmissionPackage.validate_conformance`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [datasets]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The SDTM datasets, as a dict of DataFrames keyed by domain name, such as `{"DM": dm, "AE": ae}`. The names are case-insensitive. The DataFrames can be Polars, Pandas or any other kind that Narwhals supports. [version]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["3-4"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The version of SDTMIG, as `"3-4"` or `"3.4"`. Only version 3.4 has a bundled catalog. The default is `"3-4"`. [ct_packages]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The bundled controlled terminology packages for the codelist checks, as a list of names such as `["sdtm-ct-2024-09-27"]`. The default is the latest bundled package, which is `"sdtm-ct-2024-09-27"`. [define_xml]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The study's Define-XML, as a path to a `define.xml` file or as a [`MetadataPackage`](`pointblank.MetadataPackage`) from [`import_metadata()`](`pointblank.import_metadata`). The default is `None`, which makes the 12 Define-XML rules not applicable. [study_id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A study identifier, which is kept in the report's `package`. It isn't used by the rules and isn't shown in the report. The default is `None`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ConformanceReport]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The report, whose [`is_rules`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.is_rules`) is `True`. In a notebook it is shown as the table of [`get_tabular_report()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.get_tabular_report`). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If there is no bundled catalog for the `version`. The error message lists the versions that have one. [FileNotFoundError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If one of the `ct_packages` isn't bundled with Pointblank. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Here is a DM dataset with all the variables that SDTMIG requires for DM, but with three problems: the second subject's `RFSTDTC` isn't an ISO 8601 date, and the third subject has a negative `AGE` and a `SEX` of `"FEMALE"` (the SEX codelist has `"F"`): ::: {#09b96476 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl dm = pl.DataFrame( { "STUDYID": ["STUDY01"] * 3, "DOMAIN": ["DM"] * 3, "USUBJID": ["STUDY01-001", "STUDY01-002", "STUDY01-003"], "SUBJID": ["001", "002", "003"], "RFSTDTC": ["2024-01-15", "15JAN2024", "2024-01-17"], "RFENDTC": ["2024-06-15", "2024-06-16", "2024-06-17"], "SITEID": ["S01", "S01", "S02"], "AGE": [34, 51, -38], "AGEU": ["YEARS"] * 3, "SEX": ["M", "F", "FEMALE"], "RACE": ["WHITE", "ASIAN", "WHITE"], "ARMCD": ["DRUGA", "PBO", "DRUGA"], "ARM": ["Drug A", "Placebo", "Drug A"], "ACTARMCD": ["DRUGA", "PBO", "DRUGA"], "ACTARM": ["Drug A", "Placebo", "Drug A"], "COUNTRY": ["USA", "USA", "CAN"], } ) report = pb.validate_sdtmig({"DM": dm}) print(report) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ConformanceReport (Built-in Rules) sdtmig 3-4 362 rules (fail=5, not_applicable=12, pass=345) 5 issues — FAIL ``` ::: ::: Five rules fail, and the 12 Define-XML rules are not applicable. Let's see which rules failed: ::: {#ad81af39 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} for rule in report.rules(status="fail"): print(rule.rule_id, rule.sensitivity, rule.message) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` SDTM-007 Error SEX value is not in the SEX codelist. SDTM-011 Error RFSTDTC does not conform to ISO 8601 extended datetime format. SDTM-121 Error Required domain(s) missing: TS SDTM-122 Warning Required domain(s) missing: TA SDTM-195 Error AGE must not be negative in DM. ``` ::: ::: The three problems are each found by a rule. The other two failures are for the TS and TA datasets, which every SDTM submission needs. The failing records can be had as a DataFrame with [`findings_df()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.findings_df`) or as a table with [`get_findings_table()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.get_findings_table`). With a Define-XML, the Define-XML rules are run as well. Pointblank comes with a DM dataset as an XPT file and a Define-XML for it: ::: {#ff2ea766 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pyreadstat dm, _ = pyreadstat.read_xport(pb.load_metadata_example("dm.xpt")) report = pb.validate_sdtmig({"DM": dm}, define_xml=pb.load_metadata_example("define.xml")) print(report) print([rule.rule_id for rule in report.rules(status="fail")]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ConformanceReport (Built-in Rules) sdtmig 3-4 362 rules (fail=7, pass=355) 7 issues — FAIL ['SDTM-008', 'SDTM-032', 'SDTM-034', 'SDTM-035', 'SDTM-057', 'SDTM-121', 'SDTM-122'] ``` ::: ::: No rules are not applicable now. SDTM-057 is one of the Define-XML rules, and it finds a `RACE` of `"BLACK"`, which isn't in the codelist that the Define-XML declares for `RACE`. SDTM-008 finds the same value with the CDISC RACE codelist, and the other failures are for missing variables (such as `COUNTRY`) and the missing TS and TA datasets. The dataset was read as a Pandas DataFrame, which works as well as a Polars one. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~ConformanceReport`) : The report that is returned. [](`~validate_cdisc_submission`) : Check a submission with the CDISC CORE engine. [](`~SubmissionPackage`) : A set of datasets to check together. [](`~validate_sdtm`) : Build a validation plan for one dataset from an SDTM template.
